title: Goan-Style Cod Curry with Lime
summary: A bright, coconut-rich Goan-inspired fish curry with gentle heat, warm spices and tamarind-like sourness from fresh lime. It makes a fragrant pescatarian dinner with rice or flatbread.

ingredients.name: cod fillets, cut into large chunks
lime juice, plus extra to taste

steps: Pat the cod chunks dry and season them with 0.25 tsp of the salt, the black pepper and 1 tbsp of the lime juice. Set aside while you start the curry base.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wide saucepan over a medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring often, until soft and lightly golden at the edges.
Add the garlic, ginger and chilli and cook for 1 minute until fragrant, taking care not to let the garlic brown.

Stir in the cumin, ground coriander, turmeric, paprika and cayenne. Cook for 30 seconds, then add the chopped tomatoes and remaining 0.75 tsp salt. Cook for 5 minutes until the tomatoes have softened and the oil begins to separate slightly from the paste.
Pour in the coconut milk and 2 tbsp lime juice. Stir well, bring to a gentle simmer, then cook uncovered for 5 minutes so the sauce thickens slightly and turns a deep golden orange.

Nestle the cod chunks into the sauce in a single layer. Simmer gently for 6–8 minutes, spooning sauce over the fish once or twice, until the cod is opaque and flakes easily; avoid boiling hard or the fish may break up.
Taste the curry and add an extra squeeze of lime if you want a sharper, tamarind-like tang. Scatter with chopped coriander and serve hot.
